samples.summary: `@claude rerun` and `@claude loop` re-run only the NEWEST CI run for the head SHA, which can no longer clear gate 1 now that EVERY CI run must be green
samples.evidence: .github/workflows/agent-rerun.yml:186-190 (`listWorkflowRuns({ workflow_id: 'ci.yml', head_sha, per_page: 1 })` → `workflow_runs[0]` → `reRunWorkflow`) and the identical block in .github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:142-146. Both are the documented recovery path ("Re-running CI now; the review panel will run again and can promote or fix this PR", agent-rerun.yml:204). Under the old `ciPassed` rule the newest CI run won, so re-running the newest run was sufficient to make gate 1 pass. `ciConclusion` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:84-90) now requires *every* run of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the SHA to have concluded `success`. ci.yml has no `concurrency:` block and `pull_request` fires on `reopened`, so a SHA can legitimately carry two runs (e.g. a flaky red run, then a fresh run after a close/reopen, or a manually cancelled run). Once an older run for the head SHA is red/cancelled, re-running only `workflow_runs[0]` leaves it red forever: gate 1 becomes permanently unsatisfiable for that SHA, `mark-ready` exits 1 on every round, and both commands still tell the human the panel "can promote". The fix belongs at these two call sites (re-run every non-success CI run for the SHA, i.e. iterate over `ciRunsFor`), not necessarily on the new rule.

samples.summary: The CI-run identity rule now exists in four copies with two different semantics: the YAML gates compare the path with strict equality, while `ciRunsFor` deliberately strips an `@ref` suffix
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/checks.mjs:61-62 strips `@<ref>` (`String(r?.path ?? "").split("@")[0]`) because "called workflows report `path` with an `@ref` suffix", and mark-ready.test.mjs:246-256 pins that tolerance. The three workflow guards do not: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:54, .github/workflows/ci-report.yml:56 and .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:117/166 all use `== '.github/workflows/ci.yml'`. If the `@ref` form the JS code accommodates ever appears (CI invoked as a called workflow), the three workflow gates refuse every real CI run and the panel, the CI-fix arm and the CI report all go silent while the JS gate keeps working — the failure mode is a pipeline that stops with no error. Secondly, the literal in agent-iterate-ci.yml:54 and ci-report.yml:56 is tied to nothing: checks.test.mjs pins only agent-review-panel.yml (via the PATH substitution at checks.test.mjs:181) and asserts only that the file exists (checks.test.mjs:443-453), so renaming ci.yml would silently disable those two workflows.

samples.summary: The second consumer of `ciConclusion` (state projection) silently reclassifies PRs whose head SHA has more than one CI run
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:226-228 feeds `ciConclusion(runs)` into `deriveState` (scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:129-130). Previously the newest CI run for the SHA decided the signal; now any single non-success run (red, cancelled, skipped) makes the signal `"failure"`, so `deriveState` returns `awaiting-ci` where it used to return `reviewing`. The reconcile path (agent-review-panel.yml:2465, `set-state.mjs reconcile`) will therefore relabel such a PR `agent:awaiting-ci` even after a later CI run for the same SHA went green — the label a human reads, and the same SHA on which `mark-ready` gate 1 has become permanently unsatisfiable. Nothing in set-state.test.mjs exercises `gatherSignals`, so this consumer change is unpinned; the call site that needs a decision about it is this line.

samples.summary: Sibling `workflow_run` consumers still identify their producer by display name only; capture-collect's is the one holding a cross-repo write token
searchedFor: read docker-publish.yml if:, publish-ghpage.yml if:, capture-collect.yml if:
grep 'path' in the three unhardened workflows
samples.evidence: The diff's own rationale is that `workflows:` matches a forgeable display name. Three of the five consumers were hardened; the others were not. .github/workflows/capture-collect.yml:68 subscribes to `["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]` and its only gate is `conclusion != 'skipped'` (capture-collect.yml:129) — no `path`, no `head_repository` check — while the job checks out `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN` (capture-collect.yml:142-146). A workflow file on any same-repo PR branch named `Agent Review Panel` therefore triggers a token-bearing store-pushing run. Impact is limited because the collector selects artifacts by name prefix over a 7-day window rather than from the triggering run (scripts/agent/collect-captures.mjs:438,650), so a forged trigger buys an extra sweep, not a chosen payload. docker-publish.yml:66-70 and publish-ghpage.yml:41-47 are likewise display-name-only, mitigated (as the diff notes) by `head_branch == 'main' && event == 'push'` — though a second `name: CI` file merged to main would then deploy/publish main on its own green conclusion.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence checks out in the repo. scripts/agent/checks.mjs:84-89 implements ciConclusion as "every CI run for the SHA must be success" (fail-closed replacement of newest-wins), and it is the sole source of gate 1 via scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:138 (and set-state.mjs:228). The two remediation call sites still assume the old semantics: .github/workflows/agent-rerun.yml:186-190 and .github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:142-146 both call listWorkflowRuns with per_page: 1 and re-run only workflow_runs[0] (newest-first ordering), then tell the human at agent-rerun.yml:204 / agent-loop.yml:153 that CI is re-running and the panel "can promote". Since a re-run adds a run_attempt to that one run only (as checks.mjs:70-73 itself notes), any older non-success CI run for the same head SHA stays red and gate 1 becomes unsatisfiable for that SHA while the command reports success. Reachability is real: .github/workflows/ci.yml has no concurrency: block and its pull_request trigger (line 9) declares no types:, so the default set includes reopened, and push/merge_group are additional triggers — nothing stops one head SHA carrying two runs of that workflow file. This is the blast-radius lane (behaviour change to an exported symbol with unupdated consumers outside the diff), and I found no guard or alternative re-run-all path that makes it unreachable.

finding.summary: The `name: CI` spoof this delta closes in mark-ready is still wide open in every `workflow_run` trigger that consumes CI — including the two jobs that push commits with contents:write
finding.evidence:
The delta's stated threat model (checks.mjs:41-56, mark-ready.mjs:133-136, docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1904-1916) is: "anyone able to push a branch to the base repo could add `.github/workflows/anything.yml` with `name: CI` on `push`, get a green run recorded against their own head SHA". Gate 1 now matches on `path`, but every other reader of CI still matches on the run's display name and cannot be fixed by this constant:
- `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:28` — `workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"]`
- `.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:21` — same
- `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:19`, `.github/workflows/publish-ghpage.yml:22`, `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:25` — same
The promote path is now protected (mark-ready re-derives gate 1 from the path), but the panel's `fix` job (agent-review-panel.yml:1618-1636, `contents: write`, gated only on `needs.ci.outputs.conclusion == 'success'`, where that conclusion is read off `context.payload.workflow_run.id` at agent-review-panel.yml:291 without ever checking which file produced it) and `agent-iterate-ci.yml` are still driven by a name-matched run. A forged workflow file named `CI` on a branch therefore still starts the LLM fixer, which pushes commits. `github.event.workflow_run.path` is available in the payload and the `ci`/`gate` jobs could assert it against `CI_WORKFLOW_PATH`; the fix belongs in those workflows, not in checks.mjs.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the `name: CI` spoof remains open in every workflow_run consumer of CI, specifically that the panel's `fix` job and `agent-iterate-ci.yml` are driven by a purely name-matched run. Both are in fact path-guarded. In agent-review-panel.yml the `gate` job asserts `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` (line 166, rationale lines 156-163); `ci` (line 277-278) and `review-panel` (line 374-375) both depend on `gate` and on `needs.gate.outputs.managed == 'true'`, and `fix` (contents: write, line 1646) is `needs: [review-panel, ci]` with a non-`always()` `if` (lines 1638-1641) — so a forged run skips `gate` and every downstream pushing job with it. `stalled` (line 2322) also cannot fire on a skipped `gate`. agent-iterate-ci.yml asserts the same path at line 54, with its contents:write `iterate` job `needs: [gate]` (line 87). ci-report.yml asserts the path at line 56. docker-publish.yml (lines 18-21, 51-60) and publish-ghpage.yml (lines 21-24, 41-47) lack a path clause but require `event == 'push' && head_branch == 'main' && head_repository == github.repository`, so a forgery would have to be merged to main first, and neither pushes commits. The described bypass to the LLM fixer does not exist in this tree.
